Eratosthenes (born 276 BC) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these four has been around longest?
Fortran (founded 1957) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these four came first?
MATLAB (founded 1984) is the earliest of the four. MATLAB (Matrix Laboratory) is a proprietary multi-paradigm programming language and numeric computing environment developed by MathWorks.
Which of these four is a physicist?
Who among these is a chemist?
Stephanie Kwolek is a chemist. Stephanie Louise Kwolek (July 31, 1923 – June 18, 2014) was a Polish-American chemist known for inventing Kevlar (poly-paraphenylene terephthalamide).
What is the atomic number of Tennessine?
Tennessine is a synthetic element; it has symbol Ts and atomic number 117.
What is the atomic number of Astatine?
Astatine is a chemical element; it has symbol At and atomic number 85.
In what year did Tomitaro Makino die?
Tomitaro Makino (牧野 富太郎, Makino Tomitarō; 24 April 1862 – 18 January 1957) was a pioneer Japanese botanist noted for his taxonomic work.
In what year was Aluminium discovered?
Aluminium (the Commonwealth and preferred IUPAC name) or aluminum (North American English) is a chemical element; it has symbol Al and atomic number 13.
Which company manufactures Lockheed SR-71 Blackbird?
Lockheed SR-71 Blackbird: Skunk Works. The SR-71 was developed in the 1960s as a black project by Lockheed's Skunk Works division.
Cro-Magnon: France. Cro-Magnons produced Upper Palaeolithic cultures, the first major one being the Aurignacian, which was succeeded by the Gravettian by 30,000 years ago.
Who is credited with discovering Tucana?
Tucana: Petrus Plancius. Tucana (The Toucan) is a constellation in the southern sky, named after the toucan, a South American bird.
Who is credited with discovering Cro-Magnon?
Cro-Magnon: Louis Lartet. Cro-Magnons produced Upper Palaeolithic cultures, the first major one being the Aurignacian, which was succeeded by the Gravettian by 30,000 years ago.
Who is credited with discovering Makemake?
Makemake: Michael E. Brown. Makemake (minor-planet number 136472) is a dwarf planet orbiting the Sun in the Kuiper belt, a disc of icy bodies beyond the orbit of Neptune.
Found on every continent except Antarctica, this family of hook-billed raptors includes buzzards, vultures, and kites across 75 genera — which family is this?
Accipitridae is one of the four families within the order Accipitriformes, and is a family of small to large birds of prey with strongly hooked bills and variable morphology based on diet.
A close relative of the peach in the genus Prunus, this drupe's seed isn't a true nut and can be "blanched" by softening its skin in hot water before peeling — what is it?
This British-American theoretical physicist at the University of Illinois reshaped our understanding of superfluid helium, work crowned by the 2003 Nobel Prize in Physics — who was he?
Anthony Leggett (26 March 1938 - 8 March 2026) was a British-American theoretical physicist and professor at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign (UIUC).
This common long-term inflammatory airway disease causes wheezing, coughing, and shortness of breath that can flare into sudden attacks triggered by allergens or pollen. What condition is it?
Asthma is a common long-term inflammatory disease of the airways. It is characterized by variable and recurring symptoms and reduced lung function.
Strawberries, blackcurrants and blueberries all count in the kitchen sense — though botanists would object, since the culinary meaning of this word differs from the scientific one. What word?
Berry is a small, pulpy, and often edible fruit.

Developed in Germany from the Old English Bulldog and the now-extinct Bullenbeisser, this medium-to-large mastiff-type dog breed is known for its square muzzle, underbite, and powerful bite — name the breed?
Boxer (dog breed) is a medium to large, short-haired dog breed of mastiff-type, developed in Germany.
The leaves and buds of this evergreen shrub, when processed differently, yield green, black, oolong, white, and yellow varieties of the world's most popular hot beverage — what's the species?
Camellia sinensis is a species of evergreen shrub or small tree in the flowering plant family Theaceae.
In calculus, this formula lets you find the derivative of a composed function h(x) = z(y(x)) using the derivatives of z and y separately — what is it called?
Chain rule is a formula that expresses the derivative of the composition of two differentiable functions z and y in terms of the derivatives of z and y.
Living in a symbiotic partnership with sea anemones that shelter them from predators, these Indo-Pacific reef fish live in groups led by a dominant breeding female. What fish are they?
Clownfish (genus Amphiprion) are saltwater fish found in the warm and tropical waters of the Indo-Pacific.
Which genus of passerine birds, whose Latin name literally means 'raven,' includes about 46 species commonly known as crows, ravens, and rooks?
Corvus is a widely distributed genus of passerine birds ranging from medium-sized to large-sized in the family Corvidae.
Used to treat ADHD and narcolepsy, this 'right-handed' mirror-image form of a stimulant molecule is also misused to boost cognitive and athletic performance — what is it?
Dextroamphetamine is a central nervous system (CNS) stimulant and enantiomer of amphetamine that is used in the treatment of attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) and narcolepsy.
Long used in traditional Indigenous medicine, this prairie-dwelling genus of purple daisy relatives gets its name from a Greek word meaning 'hedgehog' — what plant is it?
Echinacea is a genus of herbaceous flowering plants in the daisy family.

Discovered in January 2005 by a Palomar Observatory team and named after a Greco-Roman goddess of strife, this trans-Neptunian object is the most massive known dwarf planet in the solar system — which one?
Eris (dwarf planet) (minor-planet number 136199) is the most massive and second-largest known dwarf planet in the Solar System.
With over two hundred species across fifty genera, this bird family includes canaries, siskins, redpolls, grosbeaks, and the Hawaiian honeycreepers — which family of seed-eating passerines?
Finch are small to medium-sized passerine birds in the family Fringillidae.
Caused by abnormalities in the genome, this category of health problem may arise from a single faulty gene, many genes, or a chromosome abnormality — what is the general term?
Genetic disorder is a health problem caused by one or more abnormalities in the genome.
Nicknamed the 'benevolent dictator for life' of the language he invented, this Dutch programmer relinquished that title in July 2018. Who is he?
Guido van Rossum (born 31 January 1956) is a Dutch programmer.
This genus of the mallow family includes several hundred species prized for their large, showy blooms, and is sometimes known by the alternate name rose mallow — name the genus?
Hibiscus is a genus of common flowering plants in the mallow family, Malvaceae.
Prized in folk medicine as an antiseptic and expectorant, this Lamiaceae shrub grows wild from Southern Europe to the Caspian Sea area — which plant is it?
Hyssopus officinalis is a shrub in the Lamiaceae or mint family native to Southern Europe, the Middle East, and the region surrounding the Caspian Sea.
This Canadian-American physical educator invented an entire sport, wrote its original rule book after moving to the United States, and founded the University of Kansas's program in 1898 — who is he?
James Naismith (November 6, 1861 - November 28, 1939) was a Canadian-American physical educator, physician, Christian chaplain, and sports coach, best known as the inventor of the game of basketball.
Cousin to the wallaby and wallaroo in the family Macropodidae, this Australian marsupial's biggest member is the red one. What is it?
Kangaroo are marsupials from the subfamily Macropodinae (macropods, meaning "large foot").

Which citrus-scented perennial herb in the mint family, whose genus name Melissa comes from the Greek for 'honey bee,' is naturalized worldwide after originating in the Mediterranean and Central Asia?
Lemon balm (Melissa officinalis) is a perennial herbaceous plant in the mint family.
This Berkeley professor upended classical logic by proposing 'fuzzy' mathematics — fuzzy sets, fuzzy logic, fuzzy control, and more — who was he?

Lotfi A. Zadeh (4 February 1921 - 6 September 2017) was a mathematician, computer scientist, electrical engineer, artificial intelligence researcher, and professor of computer science at the University of California, Berkeley.
Sharing the 1963 Nobel Prize in Physics for work on nuclear shell structure, this German-American theorist became only the second woman ever to win that prize, after Marie Curie — who was she?
Maria Goeppert Mayer (ne Goppert; June 28, 1906 - February 20, 1972) was a German-American theoretical physicist who shared the 1963 Nobel Prize in Physics with J. Hans D. Jensen.
This branch of economics studies how individuals and firms allocate scarce resources within individual markets, as opposed to the economy as a whole — what field is it?

Microeconomics is a branch of economics that studies the behavior of individuals and firms in making decisions regarding the allocation of scarce resources and the interactions among these individuals and firms.
This semiaquatic rodent can stay submerged for up to seventeen minutes, propelled mainly by its webbed hind feet while its long, scaly tail helps steer — what animal is it?
Muskrat (Ondatra zibethicus) is a medium-sized semiaquatic rodent.
A reddish-brown gas that's a key step in making nitric acid for fertilizer, it also seeps into homes from gas-stove cooking and harms indoor air — which compound, formula NO2?
Nitrogen dioxide is a chemical compound with the formula NO2.

This group of middle-ear inflammations includes a painful acute infection that makes young children tug at their ears, plus a quieter form defined by non-infectious fluid lingering for weeks. What is the condition?
Otitis media is a group of inflammatory diseases of the middle ear.
Built for the sea, it sports a spiny tongue and powerful jaws to grip slippery fish, then swallows them whole mid-swim. Which animal splits its life half on land, half in the water?
Penguin are a group of flightless semi-aquatic sea birds which live almost exclusively in the Southern Hemisphere.
Native to South America and the most economically important member of the Bromeliaceae family, this tropical 'multiple fruit' became a 17th-century European symbol of luxury — what is it?
Pineapple (Ananas comosus) is a tropical plant with an edible fruit; it is the most economically significant plant in the family Bromeliaceae.

This male sexual dysfunction occurs when orgasm happens very soon after minimal sexual stimulation, with medical experts generally setting the threshold at around one minute — what's this condition called?

Premature ejaculation (PE) is a male sexual dysfunction that occurs when a male expels semen (and most likely experiences orgasm) soon after beginning sexual activity, and with minimal penile stimulation.
This colorless, odorless radioactive noble gas has the atomic number 86, and its longest-lived isotope has a half-life of under four days — name the element?
Radon is a chemical element; it has symbol Rn and atomic number 86.
Known by the common name 'dog rose,' this climbing wild rose species is native across Europe and stretches into northwest Africa and western Asia — which species?
Rosa canina is a variable climbing, wild rose species native to Europe, northwest Africa, and western Asia.

Seven living species make up this group of ocean-dwelling reptiles, five of which are threatened with extinction — one species, found only near Australia, Papua New Guinea, and Indonesia, is not — name this group?
Sea turtle (superfamily Chelonioidea), sometimes called marine turtles, are reptiles of the order Testudines and of the suborder Cryptodira.
Whether on land, in fresh water, or in the sea, this gastropod earns its name from a coiled shell roomy enough to fully retract into — what is it?
Snail is a shelled gastropod. The name is most often applied to land snails, terrestrial pulmonate gastropod molluscs.
This group of cartilaginous fish spans eleven families and roughly 220 species, from tiny river-dwellers to giant manta and devil rays — what group of fish is it?
Stingray are a group of rays, a type of cartilaginous fish.
This fibrous connective tissue connects muscle to bone, unlike its cousin which connects bone to bone, and numbers about 4,000 throughout the adult human body — what is it?
Tendon is a tough band of dense fibrous connective tissue that connects muscle to bone.
Caused by superantigens from staph or strep bacteria, this condition brings fever, a sunburn-like rash, and peeling skin, and has been tied to absorbent tampon use — which condition?
Toxic shock syndrome (TSS) is a condition caused by bacterial toxins.
This abnormal enlargement of the vein network draining the testicles is the most common correctable cause of male infertility, found in over a third of men with the condition. Name it?
Varicocele is an abnormal enlargement of the pampiniform venous plexus in the scrotum.
This biological process unfolds in predictable phases — hemostasis, inflammation, cell proliferation, and tissue remodeling — to replace damaged skin after the barrier is broken. What is it?
Wound healing refers to a living organism's replacement of destroyed or damaged tissue by newly produced tissue.
The simplest alkyne, this colorless gas packs all four of its atoms into one straight line thanks to a carbon-carbon triple bond, and fuels welding torches — which compound is it?
First nominated by Ronald Reagan in 1987 and reappointed every four years until 2006, this soft-spoken economist logged the second-longest tenure ever as chairman of the Federal Reserve — who was he?
Alan Greenspan: American economist and financial advisor (born 1926)

Nicknamed 'lazy eye,' this childhood vision disorder occurs when the brain favors one eye over the other, and correcting the underlying cause doesn't restore sight right away — what is this condition?
Amblyopia: Failure of the brain to process input from one eye.
Comprising over 22,000 species including ragworms, earthworms, and leeches, this phylum of segmented worms use parapodia to move — what is it?
Annelid: Phylum of segmented worms. The basic annelid form consists of multiple segments called metameres.

Known only from fragmentary remains including vertebrae and a giant femur first found by a farmer in 1987, this titanosaur may be the largest land animal ever discovered, stretching up to 35 meters — which genus?
Argentinosaurus: Late Cretaceous giant sauropod dinosaur genus.
This category of illness occurs when the body's adaptive immune system mistakenly attacks its own healthy tissue, with more than 80 recognized forms identified so far — what's the category?
Autoimmune disease: Disorders of adaptive immune system. Autoimmune diseases are a separate class from autoinflammatory diseases.
Sharing its engine, transmission, and rotor system with the Huey utility helicopter, this rapidly-developed attack chopper became America's dedicated gunship escort in the Vietnam War — what is it?
Bell AH-1 Cobra: Family of attack helicopters.

A French child prodigy who wrote a treatise on conic sections at 16, then built one of the first mechanical calculators and traded letters with Fermat that helped birth probability theory — who was he?
Typically housed in the head near the organs for vision, hearing, and smell, this organ processes thought and cognition while coordinating muscle activity — which organ?
Brain: Organ central to the nervous system.
Native to the Americas from Patagonia to western Canada, members of this succulent plant family thrive in the bone-dry Atacama Desert — what are they?
Cactus: Family of mostly succulent plants, adapted to dry environments.

A German child prodigy turned director of the Göttingen Observatory, this mathematician, astronomer, and physicist made landmark contributions across number theory, algebra, statistics, and probability — who is he?
Carl Friedrich Gauss: German polymath and scholar (1777–1855)
This Italian physician who died in 1909 is considered the founder of modern criminology, arguing that 'born criminals' could be spotted by physical defects — who is he?
This complex of DNA and histone proteins packages long strands of genetic material into compact structures while controlling access for transcription, replication and repair — what is it?
Chromatin: Complex of DNA and protein in eukaryotic cells.

Triggered by an abnormal immune response to gluten found in wheat, barley, and rye, this chronic autoimmune condition mainly affects the small intestine and often causes malabsorption in children — which condition?
Coeliac disease: Autoimmune disorder. Coeliac disease (Commonwealth English) or celiac disease (American English) is a chronic autoimmune disease, mainly affecting the small intestine.
A heart disease involving reduced blood flow to cardiac muscle due to buildup of plaque in heart arteries — the most common cardiovascular disease. What is it?
Coronary artery disease: Reduction of blood flow to the heart. Procedures such as percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) or coronary artery bypass surgery (CABG) may be used in severe disease.
Named after the bladder because it was first found in urine, this amino acid carries a thiol group that lets it forge the disulfide bonds holding many proteins together. Which amino acid is it?
Cysteine: Proteinogenic amino acid. Cysteine (symbol Cys or C) is a semiessential proteinogenic amino acid with the formula HS−CH2−CH(NH2)−COOH.
Native to South and Southeast Asia, this is the sole species in its genus and lives in large, non-hierarchical clans with several breeding females — what's this wild canid called?
Dhole: Species of mammal. The dhole ( dohl; Cuon alpinus) is a canid native to South, East and Southeast Asia.

With nearly 24,000 ommatidia in each compound eye and wings usually held flat rather than folded, this iridescent flying insect is often confused with its lighter-bodied damselfly cousins — what is it?
The largest living land animal comes in three recognized species and counts mammoths and mastodons among its extinct cousins — what is it?
Elephant: Largest living land animal. The trunk is prehensile, bringing food and water to the mouth and grasping objects.
Marketed as Lexapro, this SSRI treats depression and anxiety but is exclusively sold commercially as an oxalate salt — what is it?

Escitalopram: SSRI antidepressant. It is mainly used to treat major depressive disorder, generalized anxiety disorder, panic disorder, obsessive–compulsive disorder (OCD), and social anxiety disorder.
With a black-tipped bushy tail and brownish-grey striped fur, this small wild feline lives in Scotland, Turkey, the Caucasus, and mainland forests, hunting rodents and ground birds — which species?
European wildcat: Small wild cat. The European wildcat (Felis silvestris) is a small wildcat species that was described in the late 18th century.
Spending 36 years at NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory contributing to America's robotic space missions, which Iranian-American scientist later advised high-tech startups after retiring in 2016?

In math, this concept assigns exactly one element of a codomain to each element of a domain, and was formalized via set theory by the end of the 19th century after originating as a way to describe how one varying quantity depends on another — what is it called?
Function (mathematics): Association of one output to each input.

The largest species of its kind in the world, this circumglobal sea creature was reclassified in 2017 after DNA testing showed it was more closely related to a different genus than to its smaller reef-dwelling cousin — what is it?
Giant oceanic manta ray: Species of cartilaginous fish.
Descended from medieval hunting dogs once used to take down bears, boar, and deer for German nobility, this breed ties with the Irish Wolfhound as one of the world's two largest — which breed is it?
Great Dane: German breed of dog. The Great Dane is a German breed of large mastiff-sighthound, which descends from hunting dogs of the Middle Ages used to hunt bears, wild boar, and deer.
The son of a famous physicist and his first wife, this Swiss-American engineer taught hydraulic engineering at Berkeley and became renowned for research on sediment transport — who is he?

Hans Albert Einstein: Swiss-American engineer and educator. Hans Albert Einstein (May 14, 1904 – July 26, 1973) was a Swiss-American engineer, the second child and first son of physicists Albert Einstein and Mileva Marić.
In this condition, part of the stomach slips upward through the diaphragm into the chest, often triggering acid reflux, heartburn, or trouble swallowing — what is it?
Hiatal hernia: Entrance of abdominal organs into the middle chest through the diaphragm.
Also called prussic acid, this toxic, flammable liquid with the formula HCN boils just above room temperature and serves as an industrial precursor to plastics and mining chemicals — what is it?
Native to the subcontinent, the male of this bird species is called a peacock and sports a fan-shaped crest with a dazzling train of eyespot feathers used in courtship — which species?
Indian peafowl: Species of bird. The Indian peafowl (Pavo cristatus), also known as the common peafowl, or blue peafowl, is a species of peafowl native to the Indian subcontinent.
Awarded a gas-attack Iron Cross in WWI before sharing the 1925 Nobel with Gustav Hertz for the laws of how an electron strikes an atom — who was this German-American physicist?
Hailed as a 'miracle worker' in 1955, this researcher refused to patent his polio vaccine so it could spread worldwide for free — who is he?
Jonas Salk: American inventor of the polio vaccine (1914–1995)

Also called 47,XXY, this chromosome anomaly leaves those affected phenotypically male but often infertile, and is named after the American endocrinologist who first identified it in the 1940s — what's the condition?
Called a 'universal genius,' this Swiss polymath founded graph theory and topology while introducing much of modern mathematical notation — who is he?

Developed under the US Air Force's Advanced Tactical Fighter program, this American twin-engine stealth fighter was designed for air superiority but also handles ground attack, electronic warfare and signals intelligence — which aircraft?

Lockheed Martin F-22 Raptor: American stealth air superiority fighter. The Lockheed Martin–Boeing F-22 Raptor is an American twin-engine, jet-powered, all-weather, supersonic stealth fighter aircraft.
This is the common name for the larva of flies like houseflies and blowflies — though, confusingly, not for baby mosquitoes — what is it called?
Growing out of calculus and the study of derivatives and integrals, this branch of mathematics examines functions, spaces, and limits using methods of approximation and convergence — which field?

Mathematical analysis: Branch of mathematics. Mathematical analysis is the branch of mathematics that studies functions, spaces, and operators through quantitative methods of approximation and convergence.
Sold under the brand Glucophage, this first-line oral medication for type 2 diabetes is favored partly because it isn't associated with weight gain. What drug is it?
Metformin: Medication used to treat diabetes.
Medically termed a 'spontaneous abortion,' this is the loss of an embryo or fetus before it can survive independently — distinct from a stillbirth, which occurs after 20 weeks. What is it?
Miscarriage: Natural premature termination of pregnancy.
This Austrian-School economist founded anarcho-capitalism and called the state "the organization of robbery systematized and writ large" — which libertarian theoretician?
Roughly how many Earth years does Neptune take to complete one orbit of the Sun?
Neptune orbits once every 164.8 years at about 30 astronomical units. It has completed only one full orbit since its discovery in 1846.
Built from a nitrogen-containing base, a five-carbon sugar, and a phosphate group, these molecules are the monomer building blocks of DNA and RNA — what are they called?
Nucleotide: Biological molecules constituting nucleic acids.
Nicknamed 'brittle bone disease,' this genetic disorder causes fragile bones and blue-tinted eye whites, usually stemming from faulty type I collagen — what is it?
Osteogenesis imperfecta: Group of genetic disorders resulting in fragile bones.

Native to southern Brazil, Paraguay and northern Argentina, this vine produces a round berry that turns yellow or dark purple at maturity, prized for its juicy, seed-filled interior — what is it, scientifically speaking?
Passiflora edulis: Species of flowering plant in the passion flower family.

Positioned behind the mouth and nasal cavity, this throat structure channels food toward the esophagus and air toward the larynx, with a flap of cartilage guarding against the two crossing paths — what is it?
Pharynx: Part of the throat that is behind the mouth and nasal cavity.
Connected to the fetus by the umbilical cord, this temporary organ handles nutrient and waste exchange between mother and baby during pregnancy — what is it?
Placenta: Organ that connects the fetus to the uterine wall.
Despite its common name, this burrowing rodent native to North American grasslands is actually a type of ground squirrel, not a canine — what is it?
Prairie dog: Genus of ground squirrels.
Studied by Confucius and central to rhetoric in ancient Greece and Rome, this skill involves delivering an address to a live audience — what is it called?
Public speaking: Performing a speech to a live audience.

The largest of the true foxes and the most widely distributed carnivore on Earth, this Northern Hemisphere native is so destructive where it's been introduced that it made the list of the world's 100 worst invasive species — which animal is it?
Red fox: Species of mammal. The red fox (Vulpes vulpes) is the largest of the true foxes, and the most widely distributed member of the order Carnivora.
The wild ancestor of the domestic pigeon, this pale grey bird has two black bars on each wing and gave rise to feral pigeons worldwide — what is it?
Rock dove: Ancestor of domestic pigeon. The domestic pigeon, often called "Columba livia domestica", which includes about 1,000 different breeds, is descended from this species.

A member of the mint family native to the Mediterranean, this grayish-leaved perennial subshrub is used both in cooking and as an ornamental garden plant — which herb, better known by its common name sage?
Salvia officinalis: Species of plant. Salvia officinalis, common sage or sage, is a perennial, evergreen subshrub, with woody stems, grayish leaves, and blue to purplish flowers.
Broader than linguistics, this field studies how signs — from words to maps to clothing — form systems that carry meaning, split into syntactics, semantics, and pragmatics — what is it called?
Semiotics: Study of signs. It is an interdisciplinary field that examines what signs are, how they form sign systems, and how individuals use them to communicate meaning.
These slow-moving South American mammals hang upside down in rainforest canopies, are kin to anteaters, and — despite the "two-toed" label — all have three toes on each rear limb; what are they?
Sloth: Group of tree dwelling mammals noted for slowness.
Native to China and Vietnam but now invasive across the US after spreading through South Korea and Japan, this planthopper prefers the also-invasive tree of heaven as its host — what insect is it?
Spotted lanternfly: Species of planthopper indigenous to Southeast Asia.
This bright yellow nonmetal — element 16, known since ancient times in India, Greece and China — forms cyclic eight-atom rings under normal conditions. What is it?
Sulfur: Chemical element with atomic number 16 (S)
From Greek for 'arrangement' and 'method', this science names and classifies organisms into ranked groups — domain, kingdom, phylum, and on down to species — what is the field?

Taxonomy (biology): Science of classifying organisms. The principal ranks in modern use are domain, kingdom, phylum (division is sometimes used in botany in place of phylum), class, order, family, genus, and species.

When a piece of one of these blood-vessel clots breaks free to travel the body it's called an embolus — and the original blockage can trigger a stroke or heart attack. What is this clot formation called?
Thrombosis: Formation of blood clots inside the blood vessels.
Also known as all-trans retinoic acid, this medication treats acne as a topical cream but must be taken orally for leukemia patients with a specific gene fusion — what is it?
Tretinoin: Medication. Tretinoin, also known as all-trans retinoic acid (ATRA), is a medication used for the treatment of acne and acute promyelocytic leukemia.
Known as the Great Bear, this constellation contains the seven-star pattern nicknamed the Big Dipper — what's it called?
Ursa Major: Constellation in the northern sky.
Sporting prominent tusks and whiskers, this Arctic pinniped's Pacific males can weigh over 2,000 kilograms, making it second in size among pinnipeds only to the elephant seals — what animal?
Walrus: Species of marine mammal with tusks.
Named for the Aztec god of fire and lightning, this ancient Mexican dog breed comes in hairless and fully-coated varieties within the same litter — which breed?
Xoloitzcuintle: Hairless dog breed from Mexico.
What is the chemical symbol for thallium?
The symbol for thallium is Tl. Thallium is a chemical element; it has symbol Tl and atomic number 81.
The symbol for osmium is Os. Osmium is a chemical element; it has symbol Os and atomic number 76.

In what year was Farrah Fawcett born?
Farrah Fawcett: Mary Ferrah Leni "Farrah" Fawcett (February 2, 1947 – June 25, 2009) was an American actress.
In what year was Angelina Jolie born?
Angelina Jolie ( joh-LEE; born Angelina Jolie Voight [ VOYT] on June 4, 1975) is an American actress, filmmaker, and humanitarian.
In what year was Viggo Mortensen born?
Viggo Mortensen: Viggo Peter Mortensen Jr. (Danish: [ˈviko ˈmɒːtn̩sn̩]; born October 20, 1958) is an American actor and filmmaker.
In what year was Marisa Tomei born?
Marisa Tomei (Italian: [toˈmɛi]; born December 4, 1964) is an American actress.
In what year was Steve Carell born?
Steve Carell: Steven John Carell (born August 16, 1962) is an American actor and comedian.
In what year was Natasha Lyonne born?
Natasha Lyonne: Natasha Bianca Lyonne Braunstein ( lee-OHN; born April 4, 1979) is an American actress, director, comedian, producer, writer, and tech executive.

Jason Bateman: Jason Kent Bateman (born January 14, 1969) is an American actor.
In what year was Ryuichi Sakamoto born?
Ryuichi Sakamoto: With his YMO bandmates Haruomi Hosono and Yukihiro Takahashi, Sakamoto influenced and pioneered a number of electronic music genres.
In what year was Han So-hee born?
Han So-hee: Lee So-hee (Korean: 이소희; born November 18, 1993), better known by the stage name Han So-hee (한소희), is a South Korean actress.
In what year was Hugh Laurie born?
